title: Qwen-CUA: Native Computer Use for (almost) Everything
data_curation: Rollouts run on an Alibaba Cloud ECS fleet with nearly 100,000 vCPUs and tens of thousands of concurrent environments. Environments are self-contained mock web services (with state injection, inspection, reset and session isolation) plus sandboxed everyday, professional and long-tail desktop apps populated with realistic files. About 40,000 verifiable tasks come in three classes, each with a reproducible initial state and an executable evaluator, audited to remove ambiguous or infeasible tasks: (1) environment-interaction tasks sampled from per-app feature taxonomies; (2) user-interactive tasks with a bounded-knowledge user simulator; (3) long-horizon workflows built by phase-state chaining, where each verified phase state initializes the next. Human trajectories on personalized desktops and professional software (CAD, Blender) get model-completed step-level CoT, filtered for consistency with state and action.
curriculum: Training is iterative, with several runs. In each run, failed SFT queries and weak domains drive teacher rerolls, new human trajectories and targeted data, which together form a refreshed SFT mixture. Every SFT run restarts from the same mid-training checkpoint rather than the previous agent, so gains transfer through data rather than through optimization drift. The new SFT model then calibrates the RL pool: from eight trial rollouts per query, tasks with 0 < successes < 8 are kept. SAPO RL on that pool yields the next-iteration model. OSWorld-Verified rose across generations: Qwen3-VL 38, Qwen3.5 46, Qwen3.6 62, Qwen3.7 73, Qwen-CUA 86.2. In the final RL run, held-out validation went from 0.734 to 0.770, and checkpoint 40 (update 800 of 1,000) was selected.
method: The model is a 397B-A17B Qwen MoE agent that sees only screenshots and emits keyboard/mouse actions plus wait/screenshot/terminate/call_user (no DOM, accessibility tree, shell or APIs). Context management keeps 20 active screenshots and folds older ones in blocks of 10 into text placeholders, so the prompt prefix stays stable for KV-cache reuse. RLVR assigns each trajectory a terminal state-based reward in [0,1] (partial credit where meaningful). From 20 oversampled rollouts, the first G=16 valid ones form a group-normalized advantage shared by all active tokens. SAPO replaces clipping with a smooth sigmoid gate, with tau_pos=1.0 and tau_neg=1.05 so that negative updates decay faster. Training-time slicing at 144K context reuses the inference fold operator, and each slice inherits the episode reward. Hyperparameters: 128 prompts per batch, mini-batch 32, constant LR 1e-6, one epoch, 1,000 updates, 100 turns, 2,048 tokens per turn. The run used 512 H200s (32 train / 32 rollout nodes on verl+SGLang) for about 61,440 GPU-hours.
eval_metrics: Pure screenshot+keyboard/mouse evaluation on eight benchmarks: OSWorld-Verified (360 tasks, 100 steps), OSWorld 2.0 (binary/partial completion), MyPCBench (184 tasks, rubric/perfect-task), MacAgentBench (676 tasks on 30 bare-metal Mac minis, Pass@1), Gym-Anything/CUA-World (1,295 tasks over 97 envs, strict-clean), ScienceBoard (169 tasks), WebArena, and RedTeamCUA (task success/ASR). Headline numbers for Qwen-CUA vs Qwen3.7/GPT-5.5/Opus-4.8: OSWorld-Verified 86.2 vs 73.3/78.7/83.4; OSWorld 2.0 18.5/48.4 vs 2.5/22.5 (Opus 20.3/54.8); MacAgentBench 69.2; ScienceBoard 64.50 vs 35.50; Gym-Anything 46.3 vs 33.1. Efficiency is also reported: 3,605.8 output tokens per OSWorld-Verified task.
key_results: Qwen-CUA reaches 86.2 on OSWorld-Verified, above GPT-5.5 (78.7) and Claude Opus 4.8 (83.4), and beats Qwen3.7 on all eight benchmarks. It cuts RedTeamCUA attack success from 36.6 to 16.4 while raising task success from 70.5 to 74.0. The >1T-parameter Qwen-CUA-Max lifts OSWorld-Verified to 87.6 and OSWorld 2.0 to 21.2/53.3.
evolution_note: Qwen-CUA continues the native screenshot-only agent line (UI-TARS, OpenCUA, Qwen3-VL) and builds directly on CUA-Gym's verifiable environment and task scaling and on SAPO for stable long-trajectory MoE RL. Its distinctive moves are an iterative SFT-refresh/RL-calibration loop that always restarts SFT from mid-training, and train-inference-consistent screenshot folding that reuses sparse terminal rewards. Its Bash-hybrid study (fewer turns but lower MyPCBench success) frames native computer use as the universal fallback layer for future hybrid code and GUI agents.
